issues.description: Indentation bug: `Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` is placed outside the `class Math_unary` block but the blank line was removed, and more importantly the original `@infer_global(math.exp)` decorator must still apply. The new top-level `if sys.version_info ...` block is positioned correctly *between* the class definition and the next `@infer_global(math.atan2)` decorator, but the deletion of the blank line above `if sys.version_info` and the placement risks breaking PEP 8 two-blank-lines-between-top-level convention and reviewer scanning. Re-check that `Math_unary` is still also registered for `math.exp` (it is, via the existing class-level decorator), and that the conditional rebind does not shadow it.
issues.detail: Looking at the diff in `numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py`: the blank line after the `]` closing the `cases` list was removed and replaced with `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` at module top level. The class `Math_unary` is already decorated with `@infer_global(math.exp)` (and many others above in the file). The new line `Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` re-applies the decorator to register `math.exp2` against the same class — this is functionally correct, but the conventional pattern elsewhere in the file is `@infer_global(...)` on the class. Consider instead defining a small subclass or matching the file's existing style. Not a true correctness bug, but it is stylistically inconsistent and easy to miss in review.
The diff explicitly shows `\ No newline at end of file` for the new release note. Numba's docs build and many lint configurations expect trailing newlines. Add a final newline.

issues.description: `sys` is imported in `numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py` but `numba/cpython/mathimpl.py` and `numba/np/math/mathimpl.py` use `sys.version_info` without an added import in the diff
issues.detail: The diff for `numba/cpython/mathimpl.py` and `numba/np/math/mathimpl.py` adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` but does not show an `import sys` being added. If `sys` is not already imported at the top of those files, this will raise `NameError` at import time on any Python version. The reviewer must verify the existing imports in both files; if `sys` is not already present, this is a P0 import-time failure. Additionally, the codebase already exposes `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` (used in the test file in this very PR) — the version guard should use `PYVERSION >= (3, 11)` consistently across all three files for uniformity.

issues.description: Inconsistent version-guard style: test uses `PYVERSION`, decl uses `sys.version_info`, impl files use `sys.version_info`
issues.detail: `numba/tests/test_mathlib.py` imports and uses `from numba.core.utils import PYVERSION` and gates with `PYVERSION >= (3, 11)`. The three production files use raw `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)`. Numba has a project-wide convention of using `PYVERSION` (defined in `numba/core/utils.py`) precisely so version checks are centralized. The PR should use `PYVERSION` everywhere.

issues.description: `math.exp2` registration uses class-rebind pattern (`Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)`) which mutates the class registration set and may register every Math_unary signature under math.exp2 unintentionally
issues.detail: `infer_global` typically registers the entire `ConcreteTemplate` (with all its cases) for the given key. Re-decorating the same class registers the *same* class under a second global key — this is the intended behavior for unary math intrinsics shared across `math.exp`, `math.cos`, etc. However, the rest of the file uses the decorator-on-class form. Verify that `infer_global` is idempotent under re-application and that this doesn't double-register `math.exp` or any previously decorated key. Prefer the existing pattern: `@infer_global(math.exp2)` on a tiny class (or extend the existing decorator stack on `Math_unary` if a stack pattern is used elsewhere in the file).

issues.description: No test for `math.exp2(0)` or large/edge inputs; integer overflow not tested
issues.detail: `test_exp2` reuses the same `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` as `test_exp`. `math.exp2` over `uint64` has a domain that easily overflows float64 (e.g., `exp2(1024)` overflows). The test should include 0 (exact result 1.0), a value near the float64 overflow boundary, and a negative integer (exact subnormal). Also, the values list has duplicates (`-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2`) — likely a copy-paste from `test_exp` that itself contains duplicates, propagating a minor test-smell.

issues.description: Missing NumPy-side support / consistency: `math.exp2` should likely also be reflected in NumPy-typed paths (`np.exp2`) or at minimum the parity should be documented
issues.detail: `numba/np/math/mathimpl.py` was modified, which is the NumPy-aware math impl module — good. But verify whether `np.exp2` already routes here or has separate registration in `numba/np/arrayobj.py` / ufunc mapping. If `numpy.exp2` is already supported via a different code path, this addition may be dead code in the np/math file. Confirm the registration is actually wired into a dispatch path that gets exercised.

issues.description: Release note title underline length matches the title text exactly — verify reST renders cleanly
issues.detail: `Add support for ``math.exp2``.` is 31 characters including the period; the underline `------------------------------` is 30 dashes. reST requires the underline to be at least as long as the title text. This may produce a docs build warning or error. Make the underline at least 31 characters.

issues.description: Blank line removed before `if sys.version_info` violates PEP 8 two-blank-line rule between top-level statements
issues.detail: In `numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py`, the diff shows `-` for the blank line after the `cases` list closing `]` and `+if sys.version_info...` directly underneath. Top-level blocks separated by class definitions should have two blank lines; class-internal code should have one. Restore the blank line for readability and to satisfy flake8/pycodestyle if numba's CI enforces it.

issues.description: No CPython-version note in docs/source/reference/pysupported.rst that `math.exp2` requires Python 3.11+
issues.detail: `math.exp2` was added in Python 3.11. Other entries in pysupported.rst do not generally annotate version requirements, but for a function whose support is genuinely conditional on the interpreter version, a parenthetical note or footnote would help users on Python 3.10 (still supported in some Numba versions) understand why their import works but the JIT call fails.

issues.description: `llvm.exp2` intrinsic semantics vs. `math.exp2`: confirm precision parity for all input types
issues.detail: LLVM's `llvm.exp2.f32`/`f64` intrinsics may be lowered differently per target (libm call vs. inlined approximation depending on fast-math flags). CPython's `math.exp2` calls libm `exp2`. For tiny inputs or denormals these can diverge by ULPs. The test should use `assertAlmostEqual` with an explicit tolerance, which `run_unary` likely does — verify.

dissents.topic: Should math.exp2 be gated by Python version, or registered unconditionally?

positions.position: Gate by `PYVERSION >= (3, 11)` everywhere because `math.exp2` does not exist on the `math` module in 3.10 and `infer_global(math.exp2)` would raise `AttributeError` at import time. The current PR's approach is correct in intent.

If Numba's minimum supported Python is already 3.11 (check `setup.py`/`pyproject.toml`), all version guards are dead code and should be removed. Conditional imports are technical debt the moment the floor moves above 3.11.

dissents.topic: Class-rebind vs. dedicated decorator for math.exp2 typing

positions.position: `Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` is one line and avoids defining a new class. Minimum diff, maximum reuse.

Every other unary math function in `mathdecl.py` uses `@infer_global(...)` on the class. The class-rebind form is the only non-decorator registration in the file and creates a maintenance asymmetry. Prefer `@infer_global(math.exp2)` on a (possibly trivial subclass) or extend the existing decorator stack.

dissents.topic: Where to place the version check

positions.position: Use `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` everywhere — it's the project's convention, used in the test in this very PR, and decouples from `sys`. Single source of truth.

`sys.version_info` avoids a circular-import risk in `numba.core.typing.mathdecl` (which is imported very early during numba's bootstrap). `sys` is a stdlib import with no cost; `PYVERSION` requires importing numba.core.utils which may not be safe in mathdecl.

review.summary: The PR adds `math.exp2` support via the standard unary-math-intrinsic plumbing (typing, CPython impl, NumPy-flavor impl, doc, release note, test) and is small and well-scoped for a first contribution. The most important issues to verify before merge: (1) whether `import sys` is already present at the top of `numba/cpython/mathimpl.py` and `numba/np/math/mathimpl.py` — if not, this PR breaks import on every Python version; (2) inconsistent version-guard style (`sys.version_info` in three files, `PYVERSION` in the test) should be unified to `PYVERSION`; (3) release-note file is missing a trailing newline and its reST title underline is one character short of the title. Lower-priority: the class-rebind pattern in `mathdecl.py` is stylistically out of step with the surrounding decorator-on-class convention, the test reuses `test_exp`'s slightly-duplicated value list without adding edge cases (0, overflow, large negatives) that matter more for `exp2` than `exp`, and `pysupported.rst` does not flag the 3.11+ requirement. None of the findings appear to threaten algorithmic correctness — `llvm.exp2` is the right intrinsic — but the import-time risk in the two impl files is the one P0-candidate that must be confirmed by reading the unchanged top-of-file imports.
